title: Practical Side-Channel Security Levels for PERSEUS
summary: PERSEUS yields random-probing security bounds, but its Monte Carlo refinement can saturate at high security levels; determine practical targets accounting for real-attack measurement costs.

formal_statement.body: For PERSEUS, determine which practical security levels should be targeted for side-channel resistance when the measurement cost of real attacks is taken into account. The relevant gap arises because PERSEUS can produce a tight security bound, such as $\varepsilon_U \approx 2^{-40}$ for $n=6$ shares and leakage rate $p=2^{-12}$, but its Monte Carlo refinement becomes less tight at higher leakage rates and saturates for high-security circuits, such as RPMult with $n=7$ and $p=2^{-10}$, where it yields the looser interval $2^{-40} \leq \varepsilon \leq 2^{-34}$. The unresolved task is to establish practical target security levels that relate the security parameter $\varepsilon$ to the measurement cost required for a real side-channel attack.

scope.domain: Random-probing security analysis for practical side-channel resistance using PERSEUS.
parameters: ε: security parameter whose practical target is to be calibrated
measurement cost: operational cost required for a real side-channel attack
scope.unresolved_remainder: Establish practical target security levels that relate ε to the measurement cost required for a real side-channel attack.

progress.summary: The source reports a tight PERSEUS bound for one parameter setting, then notes that its Monte Carlo refinement becomes less tight and saturates for a high-security RPMult setting. It explicitly presents practical target selection under real-attack measurement costs as a broader open question.
